speaker: zainab
text: Come here, my darling! Sit with us — we have a story for you.

speaker: zainab
text: May Allah bless you, my darling. Remember: Allah is stronger than everything — so trust in Him.

speaker: zainab
text: Welcome, my darling! Come and sit here in front of the mastaba. Grandpa Salim and I were just remembering a great story that Allah tells us in the Quran.

speaker: farmer
text: The story of the People of the Elephant! Have you heard it, my son?

speaker: player
text: No — please tell me!

speaker: zainab
text: With all my heart! Listen well — and whenever you want to ask something, just ask.

speaker: player
text: I heard about a big elephant… but what's the story?

speaker: zainab
text: That's right, there was a big elephant! Listen from the beginning, and ask us whatever you like.

speaker: zainab
text: Long ago, before our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was sent, the Kaaba stood in Makkah — the House of Allah that Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them, built. People came to it from everywhere.

speaker: player
text: Grandpa, I've heard the name “Abraha”. Who was Abraha?

speaker: farmer
text: Abraha ruled Yemen for the king of Abyssinia. He built a huge, decorated church in Sana'a, and he wanted the Arabs to leave the Kaaba and make their pilgrimage to his church instead.

speaker: player
text: And why did he want to destroy the Kaaba?

speaker: zainab
text: Because the Arabs kept loving the Kaaba and travelling to it — they would not leave it for his church. Abraha became very angry and decided to march to Makkah and tear it down.

speaker: farmer
text: So he set out with a mighty army, and with them a giant elephant. Near Makkah his soldiers took the people's camels — among them camels belonging to Abdul-Muttalib, the Prophet's ﷺ grandfather and the chief of Quraysh.

speaker: player
text: What did Abdul-Muttalib say to Abraha?

speaker: zainab
text: He went to Abraha and asked for his camels back. Abraha was surprised and said: “You talk to me about your camels, and say nothing about the House that is your religion and your fathers' religion?”

speaker: farmer
text: Abdul-Muttalib answered: “I am the owner of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.” He meant: the camels are mine, but the Kaaba has a Lord who guards it — Allah. Then he told the people of Makkah to shelter in the mountains, and he stood at the door of the Kaaba praying to Allah.

speaker: player
text: And what did the elephant do when they turned him toward Makkah?

speaker: farmer
text: In the morning they turned him toward Makkah — and he knelt down on the ground and would not go forward! Allah held him back from Makkah, as the Prophet ﷺ told us.

speaker: zainab
text: Who do you think stopped the army and protected the Kaaba?

speaker: zainab
text: Remember Abdul-Muttalib's words: “the House has a Lord who will protect it”…

speaker: zainab
text: Well done, my darling! Allah protected His House.

speaker: player
text: Grandma, what are the Ababil birds?

speaker: zainab
text: Allah sent many birds against them, flock after flock — that is what “Ababil” means. And they carried small stones.

speaker: farmer
text: The stones were “of sijjil” — clay baked hard as stone. The birds pelted them with the stones, and Allah destroyed them. They never reached the Kaaba.

speaker: player
text: What does “like eaten straw” mean?

speaker: zainab
text: “Asf” is the dry leaves and straw of the crops — like the chaff our animals eat in the field. The army became like straw that animals have chewed and dropped in pieces. That is how Allah ruined their plan.

speaker: player
text: And when was the Prophet ﷺ born?

speaker: farmer
text: In that very same year our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born — so the Arabs called it “the Year of the Elephant”. It was around the year 570 CE.

speaker: zainab
text: Allah tells us this story in a short surah called Surat Al-Fil. Come, let's listen to the verses in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: farmer
text: You see, my son? Allah protects His House, and no one is stronger than Allah — however big the army, however huge the elephant.

speaker: zainab
text: So what do we learn from this story?

speaker: zainab
text: Think: was the huge army able to destroy the Kaaba?

speaker: zainab
text: Excellent! And whenever you are afraid of something, trust in Allah — He takes care of those who rely on Him.

speaker: player
text: I'll always remember: Allah is stronger than everything!

speaker: hamdan
text: Welcome, welcome! I've just come back from a long journey with my camel.

speaker: hamdan
text: Every time you eat and are full, say: Alhamdulillah!

speaker: hamdan
text: Welcome! Do you like journeys and caravans?

speaker: hamdan
text: There was a tribe that made two great journeys every year. Would you like to hear about it?

speaker: player
text: Yes!

speaker: player
text: Where did they travel?

speaker: hamdan
text: In Makkah lived the tribe of Quraysh — the Prophet's ﷺ tribe. Makkah is a dry valley where hardly any crops grow.

speaker: hamdan
text: So their caravans travelled to Yemen in the winter and to Ash-Sham in the summer, to trade and to bring back food.

speaker: hamdan
text: And they travelled in safety, because people respected them as the people of Makkah — the neighbours of Allah's House.

speaker: hamdan
text: Who gave Quraysh their food and their safety?

speaker: hamdan
text: Camels carry the food… but who created the food and kept the road safe?

speaker: hamdan
text: That's right! Every blessing is from Allah.

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah reminded them of these blessings in Surat Quraysh — the surah right after Surat Al-Fil. Listen!

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear, so He told them to worship the Lord of this House. We do the same: we thank Allah for our food and safety, and we worship Him.

speaker: hamdan
text: When you finish a delicious meal, what do you say?

speaker: hamdan
text: We thank the One who gave us the food…

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! Alhamdulillah for every blessing.

speaker: amina
text: Peace be upon you, dear! Come and rest in the shade.

speaker: amina
text: Always tell your mum and dad what matters to you — they love you.

speaker: amina
text: Peace be upon you, dear! Sit here in the shade of the palms.

speaker: amina
text: Do you remember your dreams when you wake up?

speaker: player
text: Yes, sometimes!

speaker: player
text: No, I forget them

speaker: amina
text: There was a boy called Yusuf, the son of Prophet Ya'qub, peace be upon them both. In a dream, Yusuf saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon — all bowing down to him!

speaker: amina
text: Yusuf told his father about the dream. His father Ya'qub loved him very much and said: “My son, don't tell your brothers about your dream, in case they become jealous and plot against you.”

speaker: amina
text: Who did Yusuf tell about his dream?

speaker: amina
text: He told the one who loved him most and gave him good advice…

speaker: amina
text: Well done! He told his father.

speaker: amina
text: Allah tells us about this in Surat Yusuf. Let's listen to the two verses.

speaker: amina
text: Yusuf teaches us to share our secrets and worries with our parents, because they love us and give us good advice. And many years later, Yusuf's dream came true — a beautiful story you'll hear the rest of one day!

speaker: amina
text: If you have something important to share, who do you tell?

speaker: amina
text: Like Yusuf: who loves you most of all?

speaker: amina
text: Wonderful! That's just what Yusuf did.

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! Come — I have a story for you about two wonderful threads.

speaker: amina
text: If you don't understand something, ask someone who knows — that is how we learn.

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! I was looking out of this window at the sky before dawn. Did you know there is a verse in the Quran about a white thread and a black thread?

speaker: amina
text: Would you like to hear their story?

speaker: player
text: Yes, Grandma, tell me!

speaker: amina
text: Listen, then — and whenever a question comes to you, ask.

speaker: player
text: Threads? Like sewing threads?

speaker: amina
text: A lovely question! That is exactly what some people thought the first time. Listen to the story.

speaker: amina
text: In Ramadan we fast from dawn until sunset. The Companion Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, told that when Allah's words “eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread” were revealed, the words “of dawn” had not yet been revealed.

speaker: player
text: So what did people do when they heard that verse?

speaker: amina
text: Sahl said: when some men wanted to fast, one of them would tie a white thread and a black thread to his leg.

speaker: amina
text: And he would keep on eating until the two threads became clear enough for him to see.

speaker: player
text: A real thread on his leg? Could he see it in the dark?

speaker: amina
text: In the dark of night you can hardly tell the two threads apart. So he waited until there was enough light to tell the white from the black. That is how they understood the verse at first.

speaker: player
text: And how did they learn the right meaning?

speaker: amina
text: Afterwards Allah revealed the words “of dawn”. Sahl said: then they knew that He meant the night and the day.

speaker: amina
text: So the white thread is the whiteness of day that appears on the horizon at dawn, and the black thread is the blackness of night — a thin line of light that Allah draws across the sky every morning!

speaker: amina
text: What do the white thread and the black thread in the verse mean?

speaker: amina
text: Remember the words that came afterwards: “of dawn”…

speaker: amina
text: Well done, my darling! They are the light of dawn and the darkness of night.

speaker: player
text: So when do we stop eating suhoor?

speaker: amina
text: We eat suhoor at night — dates, water and milk — and when dawn breaks and that white thread shows on the horizon, we stop eating and drinking until sunset.

speaker: amina
text: Come, let's listen to this part of the verse in the sheikh's voice. Listen for the words “of dawn”!

speaker: amina
text: You see? The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wanted to obey Allah exactly — and when the meaning wasn't clear to them, Allah in His mercy made it clear.

speaker: amina
text: So what do we learn from this story?

speaker: amina
text: Remember: when the meaning wasn't clear to the Companions… what happened?

speaker: amina
text: Excellent! We ask people of knowledge and we learn — and Allah makes things clear for us.

speaker: player
text: I'll look at the horizon at dawn to see the white thread!

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! A long day in the field… come, I'll tell you about a fasting farmer like me.

speaker: farmer
text: Allah is merciful to us, my son — He wants ease for us.

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! Look, the sun is going down — the time when farmers go home. Did you know that a fasting farmer was the reason a verse of the Quran was revealed?

speaker: farmer
text: Would you like to hear his story?

speaker: player
text: Yes, Grandpa, tell me!

speaker: farmer
text: Listen, my son, and ask whatever you like.

speaker: player
text: A fasting farmer? Like you, Grandpa?

speaker: farmer
text: Yes — he worked his land just like me! Listen to the story.

speaker: farmer
text: Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, told that at first the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ had a fasting rule different from the one we know today.

speaker: player
text: What was that rule, Grandpa?

speaker: farmer
text: Al-Bara' said: if a man was fasting and the time to break the fast came, and he fell asleep before eating, he could not eat that night or the next day until evening.

speaker: farmer
text: That means: if sleep overcame him after sunset before he had eaten, he stayed fasting that night and the whole next day, until evening!

speaker: player
text: And who was the fasting farmer?

speaker: farmer
text: A man of the Ansar called Qays ibn Sirma, may Allah be pleased with him. He was fasting, and he worked on his land all day long.

speaker: player
text: What happened when it was time to break the fast?

speaker: farmer
text: He came to his wife and asked her: “Do you have any food?” She said: “No — but I will go and look for some for you.”

speaker: farmer
text: He had been working all day, and his eyes overcame him — he fell asleep before he had eaten anything.

speaker: player
text: Poor man! Did he have to keep fasting the next day?

speaker: farmer
text: Yes. By midday he fainted from exhaustion — and this was told to the Prophet ﷺ.

speaker: farmer
text: What do you think Allah revealed, out of mercy for people?

speaker: farmer
text: Allah is merciful to His servants and wants ease for them…

speaker: farmer
text: Well done! And so it was revealed: “And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread.”

speaker: farmer
text: Al-Bara' said: they were overjoyed. From then on a fasting person could eat and drink the whole night — even if he slept and woke up again — until dawn.

speaker: farmer
text: This is the very verse Grandma Amina told you about. Listen to it again in the sheikh's voice, and remember Qays, the fasting farmer.

speaker: farmer
text: Fasting is a great act of worship, and Allah made it easy for us. He is merciful to His servants — He wants ease for them, not hardship.

speaker: farmer
text: So what do we learn from the story of Qays, may Allah be pleased with him?

speaker: farmer
text: Remember how happy the Companions were when the verse came…

speaker: farmer
text: Excellent! We thank Allah for His mercy — and we value the hard work of farmers and everyone who works hard.

speaker: player
text: Alhamdulillah that Allah is so merciful to us!

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Come into the palms' shade — the dates are ripe!

speaker: hamdan
text: Give others what you would love to be given.

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Look at these clusters — how lovely dates are when they ripen! Grandpa Salim and I were remembering a story about dates, and a verse of the Quran that came down about it.

speaker: farmer
text: Do you know what a “qinw” is, my son?

speaker: player
text: No, what is it?

speaker: farmer
text: A qinw is a date cluster: the big bunch of dates as it grows on the palm, stalks and all.

speaker: player
text: A bunch of dates!

speaker: farmer
text: Well done! A qinw is a date cluster — the big bunch of dates, just as it is cut from the palm.

speaker: hamdan
text: Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “It was revealed about us, the Ansar. We were people of palm groves.”

speaker: player
text: What did they do with their dates?

speaker: hamdan
text: Al-Bara' said: each man brought from his palms as much as he had, a lot or a little. He would bring a cluster or two and hang it up in the mosque.

speaker: farmer
text: In the mosque there were poor people who had no food — “the people of the Suffah”. When one of them was hungry he went to a cluster and tapped it with his stick, and the dates fell down for him to eat.

speaker: player
text: How lovely! Were all the clusters good?

speaker: farmer
text: No, my son. Al-Bara' said: some people who did not care for doing good would bring a cluster full of shees and hashaf, or a broken cluster, and hang it up.

speaker: hamdan
text: Shees are shrivelled dates that never filled out, and hashaf are dry, poor dates. In other words: they gave the worst they had!

speaker: player
text: What did Allah reveal about that?

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah revealed a verse telling the believers to give from the good things — the best of what they earn and of what He brings out of the earth for them — and not to pick out the bad to give away.

speaker: farmer
text: And they themselves would never take such poor stuff unless they closed their eyes to it.

speaker: player
text: What did al-Bara' say after that?

speaker: hamdan
text: He said: “If one of you were given the same as what he gave, he would only take it with his eyes shut, or out of shyness.”

speaker: farmer
text: Al-Bara' said: “After that, each man brought the best of what he had.” Everyone brought his finest dates!

speaker: hamdan
text: If someone gave you dry, broken dates as a gift, would you be happy with them?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember al-Bara's words: “only with his eyes shut, or out of shyness”…

speaker: hamdan
text: Right! So we never give others what we wouldn't accept for ourselves.

speaker: farmer
text: Come, let's listen to the verse in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: hamdan
text: So, little one, whenever you give charity or a gift, choose the best: the shiny, plump date — not the dry, broken one.

speaker: farmer
text: So what do we learn from this story?

speaker: farmer
text: Think: what did the Ansar bring after the verse came down?

speaker: farmer
text: Excellent! True generosity is giving your best.

speaker: player
text: I'll pick the finest cluster and give it to someone in need!

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! How do you get into your house — through the door, or over the wall?

speaker: hamdan
text: Goodness is in your heart and your good deeds — not in strange customs.

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Look at this beautiful wooden door.

speaker: hamdan
text: A quick question: how do people go into their houses?

speaker: player
text: Through the door, of course!

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! But would you believe that, long ago, at certain times some people would not go in through the door?

speaker: player
text: Through the window!

speaker: hamdan
text: No, little one! But listen: long ago, at certain times, some people would not go in through the door!

speaker: player
text: Not through the door? When was that?

speaker: hamdan
text: Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “This verse was revealed about us. When the Ansar went on Hajj and came back, they would not enter their houses by the doors, but from the back.”

speaker: hamdan
text: It was an old custom from before Islam, and they thought it was “birr” — righteousness.

speaker: player
text: And then what happened?

speaker: hamdan
text: Al-Bara' said: “Then a man of the Ansar came and went in through his door — and it was as if he was blamed for it.”

speaker: hamdan
text: In other words: some people found fault with him for using the door, the normal way!

speaker: hamdan
text: What do you think — was the man who used his door wrong?

speaker: hamdan
text: Does going in the back way bring us closer to Allah? Think…

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! And that is exactly what Allah made clear in the Quran.

speaker: player
text: What did Allah reveal?

speaker: hamdan
text: The verse came down: righteousness is not entering houses from the back — righteousness is being mindful of Allah; so enter houses by their doors.

speaker: player
text: So what is real righteousness?

speaker: hamdan
text: Righteousness is taqwa: obeying Allah, being mindful of Him and doing good. Strange customs that Allah never commanded are not righteousness.

speaker: hamdan
text: Come, let's hear the verse in the sheikh's voice. Listen for “so enter houses by their doors”.

speaker: hamdan
text: At the start of the verse Allah mentions the new moons — the crescent we see at the start of every month — as a way for people to tell the times, and the time of Hajj.

speaker: hamdan
text: So what do we learn from this story?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember: what does the verse say righteousness is?

speaker: hamdan
text: Excellent! And we are never ashamed of doing what is right, even if some people blame us.

speaker: player
text: From today I'll always use the door — and say Bismillah!

speaker: farmer
text: Peace be upon you, my son! A wide courtyard… a lovely place to pray.

speaker: farmer
text: Hurry to obey Allah — He never lets your good deeds go to waste.

speaker: farmer
text: Peace be upon you, my son! Here we are in a wide courtyard — a lovely place to pray.

speaker: farmer
text: Tell me: which way do we face when we pray?

speaker: player
text: Toward the Kaaba in Makkah!

speaker: farmer
text: Well done! The Kaaba is our qibla. But did you know the Muslims once prayed toward somewhere else for a while?

speaker: player
text: I don't know…

speaker: farmer
text: We face the Kaaba in Makkah — it is our qibla. But did you know the Muslims once prayed toward somewhere else for a while?

speaker: player
text: Which way did they pray?

speaker: hamdan
text: Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, told that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for sixteen or seventeen months.

speaker: farmer
text: Bayt al-Maqdis is where the blessed al-Aqsa Mosque is — and this was after the Prophet ﷺ had moved to Madinah.

speaker: player
text: Which qibla did the Prophet ﷺ love?

speaker: farmer
text: Al-Bara' said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved to be turned toward the Kaaba.

speaker: hamdan
text: So Allah revealed: “We have seen the turning of your face toward the heaven” — Allah saw His Prophet ﷺ lifting his face to the sky, waiting for his Lord's command — and He told him to face the Sacred Mosque in prayer. So he turned toward the Kaaba.

speaker: player
text: How did people find out the qibla had changed?

speaker: hamdan
text: Al-Bara' said: a man prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, then went out after the prayer and passed by some of the Ansar who were praying 'Asr, facing Bayt al-Maqdis.

speaker: farmer
text: He told them he bore witness that he had prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he had turned toward the Kaaba.

speaker: player
text: What did they do, in the middle of their prayer?

speaker: farmer
text: Al-Bara' said: the people turned round until they were facing the Kaaba. They turned while still praying — they didn't even wait to finish!

speaker: hamdan
text: Why did the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, turn at once, right in the middle of the prayer?

speaker: hamdan
text: Think: Allah's command came… what does a believer do?

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! They hurried to obey Allah straight away.

speaker: player
text: And what about the prayers of people who died before the qibla changed?

speaker: farmer
text: People really did ask that! And Allah revealed: “Allah would never let your faith go to waste” — meaning the prayers they had prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis were not lost. Allah never lets anyone's good deeds go to waste.

speaker: hamdan
text: Come, let's hear the verse that changed the qibla, in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: farmer
text: Ever since, Muslims all over the world face the Kaaba in every prayer — and here in this courtyard, we face it too.

speaker: farmer
text: Remember what the Ansar did during 'Asr prayer…

speaker: farmer
text: Excellent! We obey Allah with love and without delay, trusting that He never wastes our deeds.

speaker: player
text: When I pray I'll face the Kaaba — and I'll hurry to obey Allah!

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! Look at the lamp by the door… it reminds me of a story about a guest.

speaker: amina
text: Honour your guests, my darling, and put others before yourself.

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! Come closer. Look at this lamp glowing by the door. We have a story for you about a lamp that was put out on purpose!

speaker: farmer
text: Do you know why someone would put out their lamp while they had a guest?

speaker: player
text: No! Why?

speaker: amina
text: Listen to the story and you'll find out the secret.

speaker: player
text: So they could sleep?

speaker: farmer
text: No, my son! There was a beautiful secret. Listen to the story.

speaker: farmer
text: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, told that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ in need of food. The Prophet ﷺ sent word to his wives' homes, and they said: “We have nothing but water.”

speaker: player
text: Nothing but water?! So what did the Prophet ﷺ do?

speaker: amina
text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Who will take in — or host — this man?” A man of the Ansar said: “I will.”

speaker: farmer
text: He took him home to his wife and said: “Honour the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”

speaker: player
text: Did they have lots of food?

speaker: amina
text: No, my darling. His wife said: “We have nothing but my children's food” — just a little, enough only for their young children.

speaker: player
text: Oh my! So what did they do?

speaker: farmer
text: He said to her: “Get your food ready, light your lamp, and put the children to bed if they ask for supper.”

speaker: amina
text: So she got the food ready, lit the lamp, put the little ones to bed, and they set the food before the guest.

speaker: player
text: And why was the lamp put out?

speaker: amina
text: Then she stood up as if to fix the lamp — and put it out! And the two of them made the guest think they were eating with him.

speaker: farmer
text: That was the secret! In the dark the guest couldn't see that they weren't eating — so he could eat without feeling shy.

speaker: player
text: And them… what did they eat?

speaker: amina
text: Abu Hurayrah said: they spent the night hungry. They put their guest before themselves — and that is called “ithar”, preferring others.

speaker: farmer
text: Why did the woman put out the lamp?

speaker: farmer
text: Remember: there was only a little food, and they wanted the guest to eat comfortably…

speaker: farmer
text: Well done! They wanted to honour their guest without embarrassing him.

speaker: player
text: What happened in the morning?

speaker: farmer
text: In the morning the man went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah laughed tonight — or marvelled — at what you two did.”

speaker: amina
text: And Allah revealed a verse praising the Ansar: “they prefer others over themselves, even when they are in need.”

speaker: amina
text: Come, let's hear the verse in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: amina
text: Remember what the man and his wife did with their little food…

speaker: amina
text: Excellent! That is ithar — and Allah says of such people: “it is they who are successful.”

speaker: player
text: I'll share my food with our guests and my friends!

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Come — let me tell you about the greatest journey, and a loyal friend.

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah is always with us — so do not be sad, and do not be afraid.

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! I love travelling. But today I will tell you about a great journey: the Hijra, when our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ left Makkah for Madinah.

speaker: hamdan
text: Do you know who travelled with him on this journey?

speaker: player
text: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq?

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him — his closest companion, and the first grown man to believe in him.

speaker: player
text: No — who was it?

speaker: hamdan
text: It was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him — his closest companion, and the first grown man to believe in him.

speaker: player
text: Why was he called “al-Siddiq”?

speaker: hamdan
text: Because he believed the Prophet ﷺ in everything he told from Allah, without hesitating. “Siddiq” means someone who is always truthful and always believes the truth.

speaker: player
text: Why did the Prophet ﷺ leave Makkah?

speaker: hamdan
text: Because many people in Makkah hurt him and the Muslims, and tried to stop him calling people to Allah. So Allah allowed him to emigrate to Madinah, where the believers there were waiting for him.

speaker: player
text: How did Abu Bakr get ready for the journey?

speaker: hamdan
text: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, told that Abu Bakr had two camels ready for the road, and they hired a man who knew the way well to guide them.

speaker: hamdan
text: And her sister Asma', Abu Bakr's daughter, cut a piece from her belt to tie the mouth of the food bag — so she was called “the one with the two belts”.

speaker: player
text: Where did they hide?

speaker: hamdan
text: In a cave in a mountain called Thawr, near Makkah. They stayed there three nights.

speaker: hamdan
text: Abdullah, Abu Bakr's clever young son, spent the nights with them and brought them the news, then went back to Makkah before dawn. And 'Amir ibn Fuhayra grazed sheep nearby, so they could drink their milk.

speaker: player
text: Did anyone come looking for them?

speaker: hamdan
text: Yes — people from Makkah went out searching, until they were standing right above the cave! Abu Bakr said: “O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us.”

speaker: hamdan
text: The Prophet ﷺ said: “What do you think, Abu Bakr, of two when Allah is the third of them?” Meaning: don’t be afraid — Allah is with us, protecting us.

speaker: hamdan
text: What did the Prophet ﷺ tell Abu Bakr in the cave?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember: who was “the third” with them in the cave?

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! Allah was with them, protecting them — and no one saw them.

speaker: player
text: Did they reach Madinah?

speaker: hamdan
text: Yes. Allah kept them safe until they reached Madinah, and its people welcomed them with great joy. All along the way, Abu Bakr looked after the Prophet's ﷺ comfort and served him himself.

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah mentions this moment in the Quran: “the second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: Do not be sad, Allah is with us.” Come, let’s hear the verse in the sheikh’s voice.

speaker: hamdan
text: So what do we learn from the story of the cave?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember what the Prophet ﷺ told his companion — and did Abu Bakr ever leave him?

speaker: hamdan
text: Excellent! And Abu Bakr was a loyal friend who stayed with his companion in the hardest time.

speaker: player
text: When I'm afraid I'll remember: Allah is with us!

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! The market is busy today… it reminds me of a story that happened in the market of Madinah.

speaker: hamdan
text: Help those in need, and ask how the people around you are doing.

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Come among the stalls. Did you know that the leader of the believers, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to go out to the market and walk among the people?

speaker: amina
text: Do you know who Umar ibn al-Khattab was?

speaker: player
text: A companion of the Prophet ﷺ?

speaker: amina
text: Yes, my darling. He was one of the Prophet's ﷺ closest companions, and became the leader of the Muslims after Abu Bakr. He was called “al-Faruq”, because he told right apart from wrong.

speaker: player
text: No — who was he?

speaker: amina
text: He was one of the Prophet's ﷺ closest companions, and became the leader of the Muslims after Abu Bakr. He was called “al-Faruq”, because he told right apart from wrong.

speaker: player
text: What was he like with people?

speaker: amina
text: He was firm about what is right and gentle with the weak. He feared Allah greatly, and he knew he would answer to Allah for the people.

speaker: player
text: What happened in the market?

speaker: hamdan
text: Aslam, Umar's helper, told: I went out with Umar to the market, and a young woman caught up with him and said: “O leader of the believers, my husband has died and left little children. They have no crops and no sheep.”

speaker: amina
text: And she said: “I am the daughter of Khufaf ibn Ima' al-Ghifari — my father was with the Prophet ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah.”

speaker: player
text: Did Umar just walk on?

speaker: hamdan
text: No! Umar stopped with her and didn't walk on. He said: “Welcome to a family close to us.” Then he went to a strong camel tied up in the yard.

speaker: amina
text: He loaded it with two big sacks full of food, put money and clothes between them, handed her the rope and said: “Lead it home — it won't run out before Allah brings you something good.”

speaker: hamdan
text: What did Umar give the woman and her children?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember what he loaded onto the strong camel…

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! He gave her plenty — enough for her children.

speaker: player
text: Didn't anyone say he gave her too much?

speaker: hamdan
text: Yes — a man said: “O leader of the believers, you gave her too much!” Umar said: her father and brother gave a great deal in serving the Muslims, and we are still benefiting from what they did.

speaker: amina
text: Meaning: good people's kindness is never forgotten — we repay it to their children.

speaker: player
text: Why did Umar care so much?

speaker: amina
text: Because Allah tells us to look after orphans and people in need. Her children had become orphans — an orphan is a child whose father has died.

speaker: amina
text: And two verses of the Quran tell us: be kind to the orphan and never harsh, and speak gently to anyone who asks you for help.

speaker: amina
text: Come, let's hear the two verses in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: amina
text: So what do we learn from the story of Umar?

speaker: amina
text: Remember what Umar did when he heard what the woman needed…

speaker: amina
text: Excellent! A true leader is kind to people and asks how they are — and you can help too.

speaker: player
text: I'll help anyone in need, and be kind to orphans!

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! Come to the well… how lovely cool water is!

speaker: farmer
text: What you give for good grows with Allah — like a grain of wheat.

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! In our village we thank Allah for this well — we drink from it and water our plants. Imagine a whole town with only one well of sweet water!

speaker: farmer
text: Have you heard of the well of Rumah?

speaker: player
text: No, Grandpa — what's its story?

speaker: farmer
text: Listen, my son — it is the story of a very generous companion.

speaker: player
text: A well in Madinah?

speaker: farmer
text: Yes! A well in Madinah, and it has a beautiful story.

speaker: player
text: Why was this well so important?

speaker: farmer
text: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, the only sweet, fresh water there was the well of Rumah. It did not belong to the Muslims, and people needed its water.

speaker: player
text: What did the Prophet ﷺ say?

speaker: farmer
text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Who will buy the well of Rumah and put his bucket in it alongside the buckets of the Muslims — for something better than it in Paradise?”

speaker: farmer
text: Meaning: whoever buys it and gives its water to everyone — drinking from it just like them — will have a far greater reward in Paradise.

speaker: player
text: Who bought it?

speaker: farmer
text: Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him! He said: “I bought it with my own money.” And he gave its water to all the Muslims.

speaker: player
text: Was Uthman generous in other ways too?

speaker: farmer
text: Yes, my son! He was one of the most generous companions. With his own money he equipped many people in a time of hardship, and he enlarged the Prophet's ﷺ mosque.

speaker: farmer
text: He was called “Dhu al-Nurayn” — the one with two lights — because he married two of the Prophet's ﷺ daughters, one after the other.

speaker: player
text: Grandpa, how does the reward of giving grow?

speaker: farmer
text: I'm a farmer — I know this well! I plant one grain of wheat and ears of wheat grow. Allah gives us an example in the Quran: one grain grows seven ears, and every ear has a hundred grains!

speaker: farmer
text: That is how Allah multiplies the reward of those who spend their money on good — and Allah multiplies it even more for whom He wills.

speaker: farmer
text: Come, let's hear this verse in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: farmer
text: In the verse's example, how many grains does one grain become?

speaker: farmer
text: Seven ears, and a hundred grains in every ear…

speaker: farmer
text: Excellent! Seven times a hundred is seven hundred — and Allah multiplies even more for whom He wills.

speaker: farmer
text: So what do we learn from the story of Uthman?

speaker: farmer
text: Remember who Uthman gave the well water to…

speaker: farmer
text: Excellent! Even a cup of water you give a thirsty person is a lovely charity.

speaker: player
text: I'll give water to the thirsty and share what I have!

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! Do you know what “amanah”, keeping a trust, means? Come — I have a story for you.

speaker: amina
text: Always give back what you were trusted with — even something small.

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! If your friend gave you his toy and said, “Keep it safe for me until I come back”… what would you do?

speaker: amina
text: Would you keep it safe and give it back?

speaker: player
text: Yes — I'd keep it safe and give it back just as it was!

speaker: amina
text: Well done! That is “amanah” — keeping a trust. Our story today is about the Prophet ﷺ and his cousin, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

speaker: player
text: Keep it for myself?

speaker: amina
text: No, my darling! We give it back to its owner — that is “amanah”. Listen to the story.

speaker: player
text: Who was Ali ibn Abi Talib?

speaker: amina
text: He was the Prophet's ﷺ cousin. He grew up in the Prophet's home as a boy, was the first boy to believe in him, and later became the fourth of the rightly guided caliphs.

speaker: player
text: What did the people of Makkah call the Prophet ﷺ?

speaker: amina
text: They called him “al-Amin” — the Trustworthy — because he never broke a trust. People even left their precious things with him to keep safe; these were called “wada’i’”, deposits.

speaker: player
text: What happened on the night of the Hijra?

speaker: amina
text: Some of the disbelievers of Makkah wanted to harm the Prophet ﷺ, so Allah allowed him to emigrate to Madinah. That night the Prophet ﷺ said to Ali: “Sleep in my bed, and cover yourself with this cloak of mine.”

speaker: amina
text: Meaning: sleep in my place and wrap yourself in my green cloak. And he reassured him that nothing bad would reach him from them.

speaker: player
text: Wasn't Ali afraid?

speaker: amina
text: Ali was brave. He loved the Prophet ﷺ and trusted his word, so he slept in his bed as he was told — and the Prophet ﷺ left safely, protected by Allah.

speaker: amina
text: In the morning they found Ali in the bed, and knew the Prophet ﷺ had already gone — Allah had spoiled their plan.

speaker: amina
text: Why did Ali sleep in the Prophet's ﷺ bed?

speaker: amina
text: Remember what the Prophet ﷺ told Ali that night…

speaker: amina
text: Well done! Ali obeyed the Prophet ﷺ with courage and love.

speaker: player
text: What happened to the deposits the Prophet ﷺ was keeping?

speaker: amina
text: Here's the beautiful part! Ali stayed in Makkah for three nights and days after the Prophet ﷺ left, giving the deposits back to their owners.

speaker: amina
text: When every trust had been returned to its owner, he emigrated too and joined the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah.

speaker: player
text: Even to the people who hurt him? He gave their things back?

speaker: amina
text: Yes, my darling! The deposits belonged to the people of Makkah, and a trust is always returned to its owner. That is what the Prophet ﷺ taught us — even in the hardest times.

speaker: amina
text: Allah commands us to do this in the Quran. Come, let's hear the beginning of the verse in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: amina
text: So what do we learn from the story of Ali?

speaker: amina
text: Remember what Ali did with the deposits before he emigrated…

speaker: amina
text: Excellent! And be “amin”, trustworthy, like our Prophet ﷺ.

speaker: player
text: I'll always keep a trust and give it back!

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! Look how wide the river is! Come — we will tell you about a great ship.

speaker: farmer
text: Keep doing good patiently, and don't mind anyone who laughs at you.

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! We farmers know how precious water is — it brings the land to life. And water is part of a great story in the Quran: the story of Nuh, peace be upon him.

speaker: hamdan
text: Do you know who Nuh, peace be upon him, was?

speaker: player
text: A prophet who built a ship?

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! He was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth, one of the five greatest messengers — and he built a ship by Allah’s command.

speaker: player
text: No — tell me!

speaker: farmer
text: With all my heart! He was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth, one of the five greatest messengers. Listen, my son.

speaker: player
text: Why did Allah send him?

speaker: farmer
text: His people worshipped idols that could neither help nor harm. So Allah sent Nuh to tell them: worship Allah alone.

speaker: hamdan
text: Nuh called them night and day, quietly and openly, and was patient with them for a very long time — a thousand years less fifty!

speaker: player
text: All those years?! Did they believe him?

speaker: farmer
text: Only a few people believed with him; most refused and made fun of him. Still, he kept calling them gently and patiently.

speaker: player
text: What did Allah tell him to do?

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah revealed to Nuh that no more of his people would believe except those who already had, and told him to build a ship — under Allah’s care and by His teaching.

speaker: farmer
text: So Nuh began building the ship from planks and nails. Every time a group of his people passed by they laughed at him — and he kept on working.

speaker: hamdan
text: What did Nuh do when his people laughed at him while he built the ship?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember: Nuh was very patient…

speaker: hamdan
text: Well done! He finished the ship and trusted in Allah.

speaker: player
text: Who went with him on the ship?

speaker: farmer
text: When Allah’s command came, He told him to take on board a pair of every kind of animal — a male and a female — and his family, and those who believed with him.

speaker: hamdan
text: And Nuh said: “Board it — in the name of Allah it sails and in the name of Allah it anchors.” Meaning: with Allah’s name the ship moves, and with Allah’s name it stops.

speaker: player
text: What happened next?

speaker: farmer
text: Rain poured down from the sky and springs burst out of the earth, and the ship sailed with them through waves like mountains — with Allah protecting everyone on board.

speaker: hamdan
text: So Allah saved Nuh and the believers with him; those who stubbornly refused were not saved.

speaker: player
text: Where did the ship stop?

speaker: hamdan
text: Allah commanded the earth to swallow its water and the sky to hold back its rain. The water went down, and the ship came to rest on a mountain called al-Judi.

speaker: farmer
text: Nuh and those with him came down with peace and blessings from Allah, and life began again.

speaker: farmer
text: Come, let's hear the two verses about boarding the ship, in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: farmer
text: So what do we learn from the story of Nuh?

speaker: farmer
text: Remember: did Nuh stop building when they laughed at him?

speaker: farmer
text: Excellent! And remember to say “Bismillah” whenever you begin something.

speaker: player
text: I'll say “Bismillah” and keep doing good patiently, like Nuh, peace be upon him!

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Do you know the story of the young man who feared no one but Allah?

speaker: hamdan
text: Think with your mind, worship Allah alone, and trust in Him.

speaker: hamdan
text: Hello, little one! Today's story is about Allah's prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him, the friend of the Most Merciful. He was a clever young man who thought with his mind and loved Allah.

speaker: farmer
text: Do you know what his people worshipped?

speaker: player
text: Idols?

speaker: farmer
text: Right, my son. They carved statues with their own hands — and then worshipped them!

speaker: player
text: No — what?

speaker: farmer
text: They carved statues with their own hands — and then worshipped them!

speaker: player
text: What did Ibrahim say to them?

speaker: hamdan
text: Ibrahim asked them: “What are these statues you are so devoted to?” They said: “We found our fathers worshipping them.”

speaker: farmer
text: He told them: your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them — He alone deserves to be worshipped.

speaker: player
text: Did they listen?

speaker: hamdan
text: No. So Ibrahim wanted to show them with their own eyes that idols are no use at all. When his people went out of town for a festival, he went to the idols…

speaker: hamdan
text: …and broke them to pieces — all except the biggest one, which he left, so that they might go back to it and ask.

speaker: player
text: Why did he leave the big idol?

speaker: farmer
text: When they came back they said: “Who did this to our gods?” They brought Ibrahim and asked him. He said: “Rather, this biggest one of them did it — so ask them, if they can speak!”

speaker: hamdan
text: He wanted them to think: how can you worship something that can't speak, and can't even protect itself? And deep down they knew the idols could not speak.

speaker: player
text: Did they believe after that?

speaker: farmer
text: Sadly, no. They got angry and stubborn, and decided to throw Ibrahim into a huge fire.

speaker: hamdan
text: But Ibrahim put his trust in Allah. He said great words: “Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to rely on.”

speaker: player
text: And what did the fire do?

speaker: hamdan
text: Here is the miracle! Allah said: “O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim!” And the fire became cool and gentle — it did not hurt him at all!

speaker: farmer
text: Fire only burns by Allah’s permission, because Allah created it. Ibrahim came out safe and sound — Allah saved him.

speaker: farmer
text: What did Allah say to the fire?

speaker: farmer
text: The fire became cool and gentle…

speaker: farmer
text: Well done! Allah has power over all things.

speaker: hamdan
text: Come, let's hear the two verses in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: hamdan
text: So what do we learn from the story of Ibrahim?

speaker: hamdan
text: Remember what Ibrahim said: “Allah is enough for us…”

speaker: hamdan
text: Excellent! And whenever you are afraid, say: “Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to rely on.”

speaker: player
text: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to rely on!

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! Look at the canal water flowing… it comes from the Nile. Come, let me tell you about a baby the Nile carried.

speaker: amina
text: Allah's promise is true — so don't be afraid, and don't be sad.

speaker: amina
text: Hello, my darling! A very long time ago, here in Egypt, on the banks of the Nile, a little baby was born who became a great prophet: Musa, peace be upon him.

speaker: amina
text: Do you know the story of Musa as a baby?

speaker: player
text: No, Grandma — tell me!

speaker: amina
text: Listen, my darling. It's a story about a mother who loved her son, and a promise from Allah.

speaker: player
text: I heard about a box on the river…

speaker: amina
text: That's right! Listen to the story from the beginning.

speaker: player
text: Why was Musa's mother afraid?

speaker: amina
text: Egypt had a cruel, proud king called Pharaoh. He was unjust to the Children of Israel and ordered his soldiers to harm their little boys.

speaker: player
text: What did Musa's mother do?

speaker: amina
text: Allah inspired her — He put it in her heart — to nurse him, and when she feared for him, to put him in a box and place it on the river.

speaker: amina
text: And Allah gave her a beautiful promise: “Do not fear and do not grieve — We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers.”

speaker: player
text: Did she really put him on the river?

speaker: amina
text: Yes. She put him in the box and let it float on the Nile, with Allah watching over him. And she told his sister: “Follow him” — walk after him and see where he goes.

speaker: amina
text: So his sister walked along the bank, watching from far away, and no one noticed her.

speaker: player
text: Where did the water take him?

speaker: amina
text: The water took him right to Pharaoh's own palace! Pharaoh's household picked him up. But Allah had placed love for him in people's hearts — everyone who saw him loved him.

speaker: amina
text: Pharaoh's wife said: “This child is a joy for me and for you. Leave him with us — perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son.”

speaker: player
text: Who fed him in the palace?

speaker: amina
text: Here's the wonder! Allah made him refuse to nurse from any woman, and the palace people didn't know what to do.

speaker: amina
text: Then his sister came and said: “Shall I show you a family who will look after him for you, and care for him sincerely?”

speaker: player
text: And he went back to his mother?!

speaker: amina
text: Yes! Allah returned him to his mother so she could nurse him. She was comforted, her sadness gone, and she knew Allah's promise is true.

speaker: amina
text: Then Musa grew up, and Allah made him one of the five greatest messengers — just as He had promised.

speaker: amina
text: Who protected baby Musa on the river?

speaker: amina
text: Remember Allah's promise to his mother: “We will return him to you”…

speaker: amina
text: Well done! Allah protected him and returned him to his mother, just as He promised.

speaker: amina
text: Come, let's hear the verse with Allah's promise to Musa's mother, in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: amina
text: Remember: did Allah's promise to Musa's mother come true?

speaker: amina
text: Excellent! And remember how much your mother loves you — just as Musa's mother loved him.

speaker: player
text: I'll trust in Allah, and love and obey my mother!

speaker: zainab
text: Come, my darling, sit in front of me in the shade of the palms. I have a story for you about a blessed palm tree.

speaker: zainab
text: Isa, peace be upon him, is the servant and messenger of Allah — love all of Allah’s prophets.

speaker: zainab
text: Hello, my darling! Sit here in the shade. Can you see the palm trees and the fresh dates? In the Quran there is a surah called “Maryam”, with a story about a blessed palm tree.

speaker: zainab
text: Do you know who Maryam was?

speaker: player
text: The mother of Isa, peace be upon him?

speaker: zainab
text: Well done, my darling! Maryam, the daughter of Imran — a good, pure woman who worshipped Allah a great deal. Allah chose her and purified her.

speaker: player
text: No — who was she?

speaker: zainab
text: She was Maryam, the daughter of Imran, mother of Allah's prophet Isa, peace be upon him — a good, pure woman whom Allah chose and purified.

speaker: player
text: What happened to Maryam?

speaker: zainab
text: While Maryam was alone, in a place away from her family, Allah sent the angel Jibril, peace be upon him, with good news: Allah would give her a pure son.

speaker: player
text: A son? But she had no husband?

speaker: zainab
text: That is exactly what Maryam asked: “How can I have a son when I have no husband?” He said: “So it will be — your Lord says: it is easy for Me.”

speaker: zainab
text: Allah can do anything: He created Adam with no father and no mother, and created Isa from a mother with no father. When He wants something, He says to it “Be!” — and it is.

speaker: player
text: Where was Isa, peace be upon him, born?

speaker: zainab
text: Maryam went to a far-away place, and the birth came to her by the trunk of a palm tree. She was tired and sad.

speaker: zainab
text: Then a voice called to her from below: “Do not be sad! Your Lord has put a little stream beneath you. And shake the trunk of the palm towards you — fresh ripe dates will fall down for you.”

speaker: player
text: Dates? Like the dates here at the oasis?

speaker: zainab
text: Yes, my darling! Maryam ate the dates and drank the water, and she was comforted and at peace.

speaker: player
text: What did people say when they saw her with the baby?

speaker: zainab
text: Maryam came back to her people carrying the baby. They were amazed and said words blaming her, because they didn't know about the miracle.

speaker: zainab
text: Maryam had promised Allah to fast from speaking that day, so she didn't speak — she pointed to the baby.

speaker: player
text: To the baby?! Can a baby talk?

speaker: zainab
text: They said: “How can we talk to a baby in the cradle?” Then Allah made baby Isa speak, and he said: “I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.”

speaker: zainab
text: And he said: “He has made me blessed wherever I am… and kind to my mother” — meaning he was good to his mother and obeyed her.

speaker: zainab
text: What were the first words Isa, peace be upon him, said in the cradle?

speaker: zainab
text: Remember: the first thing he said was that he is the servant of…

speaker: zainab
text: Well done! Isa, peace be upon him, is the servant and messenger of Allah — and Allah is One, with no partner.

speaker: zainab
text: Come, let's hear Isa's words, peace be upon him, from the Quran, in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: zainab
text: So what do we learn from the story of Maryam and Isa, peace be upon them?

speaker: zainab
text: Remember: Isa said “and kind to my mother”…

speaker: zainab
text: Excellent! Being good to your parents is one of the deeds Allah loves most.

speaker: player
text: I'll be good to my mother, and love all of Allah's prophets!

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! How peaceful it is by the hills… come, we will tell you about the person we love most.

speaker: farmer
text: Send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, always tell the truth, and be kind to those around you.

speaker: farmer
text: Hello, my son! Do you remember the story of the People of the Elephant? In that very year a blessed child was born in Makkah: Muhammad ﷺ, the last of the prophets and messengers.

speaker: amina
text: Do you know what the people of Makkah called him before he became a prophet?

speaker: player
text: The Truthful, the Trustworthy!

speaker: amina
text: Well done, my darling! They called him “al-Amin”, the Trustworthy, because he never lied and never broke a trust.

speaker: amina
text: They called him “al-Amin”, the Trustworthy, because he never lied and never broke a trust.

speaker: player
text: Did they really believe him?

speaker: farmer
text: Yes! Once he gathered them at the hill of Safa and said: “If I told you there were horsemen in the valley about to attack you, would you believe me?”

speaker: amina
text: They said: “Yes — we have never known you to say anything but the truth.” He had never lied to them, not even once.

speaker: player
text: How did the revelation first come to him?

speaker: farmer
text: He ﷺ loved to be alone in a cave on a mountain called Hira, worshipping Allah there for many nights.

speaker: farmer
text: Then in Ramadan, the angel Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him in the cave and said: “Read!”

speaker: player
text: Could he read?

speaker: amina
text: No! He ﷺ could not read or write, so he said: “I cannot read.” Then Jibril taught him the first words of the Quran ever revealed: “Read in the name of your Lord who created.”

speaker: farmer
text: He ﷺ went home, his heart trembling at the greatness of what he had seen, and said to his wife Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her: “Cover me, cover me!”

speaker: player
text: What did Khadijah say to him?

speaker: amina
text: She comforted him and said: “No, by Allah, Allah will never let you down. You keep ties with your relatives, you carry the burdens of the weak, you give to those who have nothing, you honour your guests, and you help people through hard times.”

speaker: amina
text: In other words: someone who does all this good — Allah will never abandon him.

speaker: farmer
text: What was the first word of the Quran to be revealed?

speaker: farmer
text: Jibril said to him: “… in the name of your Lord who created”

speaker: farmer
text: Well done! “Read” — that is why Muslims love knowledge and reading.

speaker: player
text: How did he treat children?

speaker: amina
text: He was very gentle with children. Once he kissed his grandson al-Hasan, and a man said: “I have ten children and I have never kissed any of them!” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.”

speaker: farmer
text: And he ﷺ would pray carrying his granddaughter Umamah: when he bowed down to the ground he put her down, and when he stood up he picked her up again.

speaker: farmer
text: Allah sent him as a mercy to all the worlds — to all people and all creation. And Allah describes him as having a truly great character.

speaker: amina
text: That is why every time we say his name, we say: “sallallahu alayhi wa sallam” — may Allah send blessings and peace upon him.

speaker: amina
text: Come, let's hear the very first verses of the Quran, in the sheikh's voice.

speaker: amina
text: So what do we learn from the life of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?

speaker: amina
text: Remember what the people of Makkah called him — and the first word revealed.

speaker: amina
text: Excellent! Allah says: “In the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example.”

speaker: player
text: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad! I will be truthful and trustworthy.

speaker: narrator
text: Let's start a new adventure!
